nrSummary.cause: Product defect — rust/corrosion on metal planters after ~4 months of indoor use
nrSummary.notes: Reviewer claims the metal herb planters rusted and deteriorated from "new to shabby chic to trash" after ~4 months of indoor herb growing (water exposure from watering). Review is marked Not a Verified Purchase with no Order ID. The complaint describes a plausible real-use scenario (metal + repeated watering = rust), but unverified status is notable.
Customer expected bright white but received cream-toned white. Also expected larger pots. No defect reported. Durability concern speculative, not based on failure.

nrSummary.cause: Expectation mismatch — perceived build quality / sturdiness
nrSummary.notes: Customer likes the color and design of the Farmhouse Napkin Holder (FM19C0347a, 5.5"x5.5" White/Brown) but feels it is not as sturdy as expected. Mixed 3-star review with no return request. Reflects genuine perception of distressed/farmhouse-style construction — the rustic distressed finish is intentional and listing imagery shows the styled appearance.

Customer received the napkin holder and found it smaller than expected and the finish appeared faded. No growing/use issues — purely an expectation mismatch on size and finish. No return mentioned. Review was created the day after the order, suggesting rapid inspection.

Notes: Customer reports item arrived broken. Amazon auto-initiated replacement which was later cancelled. Indicates item likely damaged during fulfillment or transit. No evidence of misuse or expectation mismatch.

Customer perceived center wood as unfinished and rough. Listing describes rustic and distressed style but does not clearly set expectations that the center X piece may be lighter in color and lightly textured due to natural, handcrafted wood finish. Product is functional and cosmetic only. Listing-level clarification recommended.

nrSummary.cause: Off-topic / seller-conduct review — not a verified purchase
nrSummary.notes: Reviewer (Laurbar) left a 1-star review titled 'Be AWARE!' on the Taupe Ceramic Utensil Holder (HD19B235-G). Marked 'Not a verified purchase.' Review focuses on seller's marketing claims and documentation responsiveness ('I asked for documentation and none was provided') and general concerns about ceramic glazes — not actual product experience. Content fits Community Help off-topic / seller-conduct violation criteria. Community Help case drafted citing off-topic seller-conduct content, non-verified purchase (no product receipt/use), and general category commentary unrelated to actual experience with the item.

Customer rated the Farmhouse Kitchen Utensil Holder (HD19B235-W) 3 stars. Product is fine but the narrow mouth limits what and how much can be stored. Title states 6.75 inch overall but does not disclose opening diameter. Expectation mismatch rather than defect.

Customer (Yogo) left a 3-star review titled 'Utensil holder' on the CA listing of the White Ceramic Utensil Holder (HD19B235-W) noting absence of a no-slip bottom and pricing concern. Ceramic crock product — non-slip backing is not a current product feature. Pricing portion is off-topic but review is mixed with legitimate feature feedback. CA marketplace.

nrSummary.cause: Expectation mismatch — vague 'not how it was described'
nrSummary.notes: Customer (Madison) left a 1-star review titled 'Bad' on the CA listing of the Oh Hello Doormat (XT001-7) saying only 'Not how it was described.' Order placed April 15, 2026, reviewed April 19, 2026 — fast turnaround suggests immediate dissatisfaction at receipt. No specific complaint to address. CA marketplace.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect — felt letters missing from doormat upon unboxing
nrSummary.notes: Customer received the 'Oh Hello, See Ya' doormat (SKU: XT001-7) with felt letters 'a' and '.' missing upon opening. Describes the mat as thinly and cheaply made. Review also redirects customers to a competing retailer ('Can buy a nicer quality mat for $12-15 at ^arget') — 'arget' is an obfuscated reference to Target, used to avoid keyword detection. This constitutes a Community Guidelines violation in addition to the quality complaint. Community Help case drafted and submitted.

Customer expected crisp, thin lettering identical to studio images. Natural coir printing can cause ink bleed or filled-in letter counters depending on fiber density and ink absorption. Listing images likely show idealized or lightly printed samples, while real-world texture variation was not sufficiently disclosed.

nrSummary.cause: Expectation mismatch; customer received a like-new graded/resell item but expected new condition
nrSummary.notes: Reviewer alleges the item looks nothing like the listing images and appears to have been previously used, with the box opened and repackaged before receipt. No return mentioned explicitly, but tone implies dissatisfaction with perceived deception. This is not a product defect complaint — it points to an FBA inventory integrity issue.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect (paint/finish peeling after ~4 months of use)
nrSummary.notes: Customer reports the paint on the Mint compost bin peeled after 4 months of use. No additional context provided about usage conditions (countertop vs. damp area, cleaning method, etc.). Bullet 5 states the unit is intended for indoor use or under protected outdoor space and material is galvanized steel, rust proof, but does not specifically address paint adhesion or care instructions for the painted exterior. This appears to be a legitimate durability complaint based on actual use.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect — exterior paint/coating peeling after approximately 4 months of normal use
nrSummary.notes: Customer reports paint peeled on the Mint Think Green Compost Bin (AK113-Mint, B08GB7WHF4) approximately 4 months after purchase (ordered Dec 12, 2025, reviewed May 16, 2026). This is a new failure mode for this ASIN. YTD context: three prior NRs on this SKU in 2026 — capacity mismatch (3/3), rust-like markings and lid fit (3/12), and charcoal filter mold (4/28). Paint adhesion is a separate quality vector and may warrant a supplier QC discussion with Sunway. No return mentioned in the review.

nrSummary.cause: Filter mold complaint — charcoal filter develops mold on counter
nrSummary.notes: Customer (Lady B) left a 3-star review titled 'A Good Counter Fit' on the Mint Compost Bin (AK113-Mint), praising the color but noting that the charcoal filters 'can quickly turn to mold catchers.' Order ID not available (NA — Unable to Contact Customer). Mold on charcoal filters is a known characteristic of food-waste compost bins when used in humid kitchens.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect — rust-like markings on body; lid does not fit properly
nrSummary.notes: Hannah received a Barnyard Designs 1.2-gallon compost bin (Mint, B08GB7WHF4) and reported two physical defects: rust-like markings on the front of the body, and a lid that does not fit properly to contain odors. She noted the item arrived late. She found the product visually appealing but felt the defects made the experience not worth the price. No return was mentioned. This is a 2-star review on a listing currently rated 4.4 stars with 1,178 reviews.

nrSummary.cause: Listing inaccuracy — advertised capacity of 4.5 liters does not match reported internal bucket size (~1.5L per customer)
nrSummary.notes: Customer states the listing advertises 4.5-liter capacity but the internal bucket appears to hold approximately 1.5 liters. Customer expressed significant disappointment and would have rated zero stars if not for build quality. This may indicate a listing spec error (total vs. internal capacity), or a genuine capacity discrepancy. Needs listing verification against actual product specs.
Notes: Customer states pots are “tiny” and likely only suitable for a small succulent. No defect reported. Feedback indicates size expectation mismatch rather than functional failure.

Notes: Listing clearly discloses dimensions (9” height x 5.25” diameter) and capacity (7 cups). Customer dissatisfaction is based on personal expectation of treat size capacity despite accurate and visible listing information. No defect, damage, or misrepresentation identified.

Customer's sole complaint is that the item is "very small." The product title explicitly states 6.75" — this is an expectation mismatch, not a product defect. No return mentioned, no photos, single-sentence review.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect - print/letter fading after short outdoor use
nrSummary.notes: Customer reports the letters on the Half Moon Welcome doormat (XT006-W) faded within a week of use. Title 'Discussed' likely typo for 'Disgusted'. This is a print durability complaint on an outdoor entrance mat that faces sun, rain, and foot traffic. Listing positions the product for outdoor entrance use. No return mentioned in body.

Customer (Maggie Bove Tyler) left a 3-star review titled 'Cute but…' on the Welcome Half Moon Doormat (XT006-W). Says rug is small and not as durable as others, but is keeping it for the front door and notes 'It does look nice.' Listed dimensions (30x17) are accurate in title; review reflects subjective size expectation, not a listing inaccuracy.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect — print/lettering wearing off within a couple months of use
nrSummary.notes: Customer reports the lettering on the mat is already wearing off after only a couple of months. No mention of unusual conditions or rough use. This is a print durability complaint. Seller has already reached out to the customer on March 2, 2026 per Seller Central notation.

nrSummary.cause: Expectation mismatch — product appearance does not match listing images
nrSummary.notes: Customer describes the Half Moon Hello mat (XT006-HELLO) as 'poor quality' and 'not at all like the picture.' No specific defect cited — could relate to color accuracy, texture, pile density, or print quality. Coir mat appearance can vary by lot. Review is very brief with no actionable detail. Order placed March 20, 2026.

nrSummary.cause: Expectation mismatch — customer found the canister set smaller than expected ('Pretty but small')
nrSummary.notes: Customer (Ed F.) left a 3-star review on the S/3 Abby Canisters White (CR102-S3C-W, B093LLYHBH) with title 'Small' and body 'Pretty but small.' Customer praises appearance but found the size smaller than expected. Listing already discloses exact dimensions in Bullet Point 5 with a corresponding Dimensions Photo. This is a recurring pattern across Barnyard Designs canister/storage SKUs (see Jan 2026 NR on BC301-Mint Petite Canisters with identical 'expectation mismatch — personal size assumption' root cause). No listing inaccuracy; first NR on this SKU YTD.

nrSummary.cause: Expectation mismatch — canister dimensions appear significantly larger in product images than actual in-person size
nrSummary.notes: Customer received the Barnyard Designs Flour Canister (CR102-FC-W / B093LNQHL9) and found the dimensions significantly smaller than expected based on product imagery. Also reports the lid does not seal well. Customer references awareness that others have returned this item for the same reason, suggesting this may be a recurring complaint pattern. No return mentioned for this order. Customer notes it may be adequate for a single person but too small for a family.

nrSummary.cause: False/misleading review content — claims product is 'smaller than stated' despite dimensions clearly disclosed
nrSummary.notes: Customer ordered the Rosie Utensil Holder (SKU: CR103-UWH-W, ASIN: B093LPWGX4) in February 2026 and reviewed March 28, 2026. Review states 'Smaller than stated.' However, the product listing clearly discloses dimensions as 5.5"L x 5.5"W x 6"H — stated in both the product attribute section and in a dimension callout on the hero image. The claim that the product is 'smaller than stated' is factually inaccurate and constitutes false/misleading review content per Amazon Community Guidelines. Community Help case drafted and submitted.

nrSummary.cause: Potential off-topic/wrong product review — review describes seed germination failure; product is a metal planter set (no seeds included)
nrSummary.notes: Reviewer Margarita Padilla gave 1-star with title 'Didn't grow' and body 'Only one set of seeds sprouted.' Product HD303-Red is the Barnyard Designs Indoor Herb Garden Planter Set (Tier C) — a metal windowsill plant pot set with drainage tray. This product does not include seeds. The review appears to describe seed germination performance, which is off-topic for a planter/pot set. Customer may have purchased seeds separately and applied the review to the wrong product, or received a version with sample seed packets. Community Help case drafted for potential off-topic content violation.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect / fit issue — lid sizing too tight relative to can opening
nrSummary.notes: Customer received the 1.2 Gallon White Think Green Compost Bin (AK113-White) and reports the lid is too small for the can: difficult to push on, nearly impossible to remove. She would have returned the item if it had not already been used. Recurring fit issue worth pattern-checking across recent batches.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect — mat arrived cracked through the middle
nrSummary.notes: Customer received a welcome doormat that arrived cracked straight down the middle. Review is brief with no additional context on packaging condition. The defect could be shipping damage or a manufacturing issue. No return or refund explicitly requested, though Seller Central is showing the Offer Courtesy Refund option.

Notes: Customer reports staining, water retention, and dirt buildup. Product is natural coco coir, which is thick by design and known to absorb moisture and shed natural fibers/tannins when exposed to water. Listing includes care guidance, but customer experience indicates expectation mismatch with outdoor moisture exposure.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect — coir mat coming apart after one month of light use
nrSummary.notes: Customer reports the Border Coir Mat (SKU: DMC-DBOR, ASIN: B0CQ42QR5B) began falling apart after only one month of slight use. Review is very brief and does not specify which component failed (e.g., border separation, backing delamination, coir shedding). Order placed February 19, 2026, suggesting failure within approximately 5 weeks. No return mentioned. Coir durability is a recurring category concern.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect — arrived with hole in center of mat (manufacturing defect or transit damage)
nrSummary.notes: Customer received a coir doormat with a pre-existing hole in the center. Review was posted 5 days after order placement, suggesting the defect was discovered immediately upon unboxing. Customer's concern is durability, noting the hole is in the highest-wear area. No return requested. This is the third negative review in this batch from the B0D4C98Y5L parent family (alongside Kayla and Michael Gilligan) — warrants parent-level QC review.
Customer stated doormat was "much too small"; dimensions are correctly listed (17x30). No defect or listing error identified.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect — mat tore and fell apart
nrSummary.notes: Customer reports the "Hey Y'all" coir doormat (SKU DMC-YALL) completely tore and fell apart after a couple months of front-door use, despite light use (primary entry is the garage). Order placed November 18, 2025; review left May 6, 2026 — approximately 6 months of outdoor exposure. Second durability complaint logged this batch for the same SKU.

Customer reports the whole corner of the "Hey Y'all" coir doormat (SKU DMC-YALL) broke off after barely a month of use. Order shipped March 20, 2026; review left May 2, 2026 (~6 weeks). Standard coir mat durability complaint — no evidence of misuse described. Order is within return window for follow-up.

Notes: Listing clearly discloses natural coir shedding and care instructions. However, severity described (“sheds really bad”) may indicate unit-level variance with excessive loose fibers beyond normal break-in behavior. No evidence of listing misrepresentation. Monitor for repeat complaints to assess factory QC consistency.

nrSummary.cause: Coir bristle shedding — natural product characteristic
nrSummary.notes: 1-star review on Paws coir doormat (DMC-PAWS). Customer reports significant bristle shedding every time the mat is moved or stepped on, describing it as 'a huge mess.' Bullet Point 1 already explicitly discloses: 'Light shedding is normal with all natural coir mats.' No product defect — natural characteristic of coir. Common Barnyard Designs NR pattern across coir SKUs.

nrSummary.cause: Coir shedding — excessive fiber loss reported; secondary concern re: dye bleed staining porch surface
nrSummary.notes: Reviewer reports the mat sheds an 'incredible amount' and, after reading other reviews and viewing photos of porch staining from coir dye bleed, decided to move the mat indoors to the basement. Reviewer did not request a refund. Review serves as a public signal amplifying an existing dye-bleed complaint pattern on this ASIN (B0CQ3Q92KN, DMC-PAWS, 17x30 size). Product's star rating at time of review: 4.4 stars / 1505 reviews.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect — rubber backing dye bleeding into coir fibers after rain exposure; fiber separation from backing
nrSummary.notes: Customer reports two distinct defects after outdoor rain exposure: (1) black non-slip rubber backing leaching dye residue into coir fibers causing visible discoloration, and (2) coir fibers pulling away from the backing in small clumps. Customer draws an unfavorable comparison to industrial carpet remnants. This aligns with the known coir dye bleed complaint pattern. No return mentioned. Same parent ASIN (B0D4C98Y5L) as Kayla's cracked mat review (B0CQ3R952L).

Customer dissatisfied with perceived low quality. Rubber gasket does not create an airtight seal as expected. Included spoon does not hold a full teaspoon, leading to functional disappointment. No damage or misuse indicated.
Customer felt item was too small, but 12 oz capacity is clearly printed on product image.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect — visible faint crack lines under white glaze
nrSummary.notes: Customer received FM24C0002 ceramic treat canister set and found visible faint lines beneath a thin white glaze layer. She interprets this as a broken and re-glazed item. Glaze crazing is a normal ceramic characteristic but may not be disclosed in the listing. No return filed. 'Offer Courtesy Refund' CTA visible on SC. Order created March 30, 2026.

Factory failed to pack full 2-piece set (dog container + cat container + both lids). Amazon does not verify contents of sealed units. V-Trust is the assigned QC agency and set-completeness checks were not detected prior to shipment.

nrSummary.cause: Product design defect — rubber seal prevents lid from closing properly
nrSummary.notes: Reviewer finds product cute but reports rubber seal obstructs lid closure. States it only closes properly when seal is removed, but then does not keep treats fresh. Notes that positioning the seal horizontally flat (vs. vertical as default) resolves the issue. Detailed design feedback with photo evidence referenced.
Customer reports lid extremely difficult to remove and silicone gasket seal becoming distorted or misaligned after first removal, creating perception of poor quality or defect.

Notes: Both original and replacement units showed ceramic chips with visible hand-painted cosmetic repair, indicating defective units were reworked instead of scrapped. Replacement from same inventory confirms systemic QC issue rather than isolated transit damage.

Customer (Amazon Shopper, self-identified experienced gardener) left a 1-star review on Genovese Basil (SB-BASIL) stating seeds 'produced no basil plants' and accusing them of being 'old and repackaged.' Order placed November 16, 2025; reviewed April 26, 2026 — 5+ month customer storage gap. Legitimate germination complaint based on planting attempt; freshness accusation is opinion.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect — brittle plastic base cracked when bent during unboxing; coir fiber shedding
nrSummary.notes: Customer reports the mat arrived with the plastic base cracked, which she attributes to the rigid plastic shattering when bent during shipping. She also notes significant coir fiber shedding. She specifically compliments the design while condemning the build quality. Order placed February 8, 2026; review March 15, 2026 — ~5 weeks. No return mentioned but product was effectively DOA.

Notes: Customer reports hard clumps embedded in coir fibers, excessive fiber fallout on contact, adhesive-like residue. Indicates supplier-level manufacturing defect and inadequate QC prior to shipment. Customer missed return window.

nrSummary.cause: Product performance issue — natural coir material retains moisture, causing persistent two-toned/stained appearance
nrSummary.notes: Customer reports the mat consistently stays wet on one half (the portion exposed to porch weather) and never fully dries, resulting in a two-toned appearance. This is characteristic natural coir behavior — coir absorbs and holds moisture, especially when only partially shaded. Order-to-review gap of ~8 months suggests extended use before complaint. No return mentioned.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect — coir mat staining/discoloration after water/rain exposure
nrSummary.notes: Customer reports the mat looks attractive when new but became stained after a rainstorm reached it despite being under a covered section. Discoloration rendered it unpleasant in appearance. This is consistent with coir mat moisture sensitivity — coir fibers and natural dyes can bleed or discolor when saturated. No return was mentioned.
Customer states mat is beautiful but has a visible flaw that cannot be covered. No defect or functional failure mentioned. Likely natural coir variance or cosmetic imperfection inherent to material.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect (hole in mat on arrival)
nrSummary.notes: Customer received the 24x36 Brown Border Coir Doormat (DMC-DBOR-36) and reported a hole in the mat upon arrival plus the mat being too thin. The product is 0.5 inches thick which is standard for natural coir mats and is disclosed in the listing dimensions and description. A hole upon arrival points to either an isolated manufacturing defect or in-transit damage rather than a listing accuracy issue. No return was mentioned in the review. Amazon has already offered a courtesy refund option on the review.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect — coir dye bleed when wet
nrSummary.notes: Customer reports the natural coir doormat (DMC-DBOR-36, 24x36 Brown) bled brown when exposed to rain, staining the doorway and adjacent sidewalk where water ran off. Discarded the mat after one week of use. This is a known characteristic of natural coir fiber and a recurring NR pattern for Barnyard Designs coir mats.
Customer reports mat arrived torn around the edge upon delivery. Damage visible before use. Likely occurred during shipping or handling.
Corner of coir mat broke off after ~2 months during normal handling. Indicates weak edge integrity or brittle coir bonding. Not caused by Amazon fulfillment or customer misuse.
Customer provides no specific defect, issue, or functional complaint. Statement is generic and subjective (“poor quality, not worth it”) with no supporting details.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect — dye bleed/color transfer after rain exposure
nrSummary.notes: Customer reports brown dye bled onto freshly stuccoed front porch after first rainfall. Claims $200 damage. Product listing discloses coir color release and recommends covered placement — customer may not have read prior to purchase. No return mentioned.

nrSummary.cause: Expectation mismatch — water absorption inherent to coir material
nrSummary.notes: Customer purchased the 36x72 Welcome Coir Doormat (DMC-WELDB-72) and reports the coir material absorbs and retains more moisture than expected, particularly in a shaded porch setting where drying is slow. Coir is inherently absorbent — this is a material characteristic, not a defect. Reviewer otherwise praises the mat's appearance, sturdiness, and large size.

Reviewer states mat 'sheds a lot.' Coir doormats are prone to fiber shedding, especially when new, as coir is a natural fiber material. This is a recurring complaint pattern across Barnyard Designs coir doormat SKUs. No return or replacement request mentioned.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect — fiber shedding & water absorption (coir mat)
nrSummary.notes: Reviewer states mat absorbs water and fibers go everywhere. Coir doormats are naturally porous and shed loose fibers, especially when new — this is an inherent material characteristic, not a manufacturing defect. No return or replacement mentioned.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect — coir dye bleed / dark staining + watermarking after rain exposure that did not fade after drying
nrSummary.notes: Customer reports dark staining and permanent watermarking on the mat after a rainfall. She waited for the mat to dry but the stains did not fade. Ordered Feb 20, reviewed March 22 (~30 days). Classic coir dye bleed pattern under water/rain exposure. No current listing disclosure warns about this behavior outdoors in wet conditions.

Reviewer S.M. left a 2-star review with title 'Too thin' and body 'Very thin NOT HEAVY AT ALL.' Product is the DMC-DBOR-72 coir doormat (36x72, Border). Customer expected a heavier/thicker mat based on the 'Heavy Duty' claim in the listing title. This is a common Barnyard Designs coir doormat NR pattern. No return or refund mentioned.
Customer provides no specific defect, issue, or functional complaint. Statement is generic and subjective (“poor quality, not worth it”) with no supporting details.

Listing contains explicit staining warning in bullet 1. Dedicated care instruction image included (“Keep It Dry”, “Prevent Prolonged Soaking”). Physical care insert also included with product. Customer reports staining after moisture exposure under portico. Disclosure was clear and repeated. Review reflects ignored care guidance.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect (handle arrived broken and detached from main bin)
nrSummary.notes: Customer reports the handle arrived broken and immediately detached from the main bin. Customer also states the inner bin reduces usable volume and makes composting messier. The removable inner bucket is disclosed in Bullets 1 and 2 of the listing as a cleaning feature, but the impact on effective usable capacity is not explicitly stated. Handle failure is a QC and packaging protection concern. No return is mentioned in the review but the reviewer signals strong dissatisfaction.

nrSummary.cause: Product defect - side handle detachment under normal lifting load
nrSummary.notes: Customer reports the handles on the outside of the Black Think Green Compost Bin (AK113-Black) come off constantly when she tries to pick it up. Order placed May 10, 2026; review on May 11, 2026 (next day). Customer is returning the unit. This is a structural defect complaint on the side handle attachment.

Customer expected charcoal filter to prevent fruit flies from escaping when lid is opened. Charcoal filters absorb odors only and do not prevent fruit flies originating from food waste. Product functioning as designed.
Customer reported black spot near printed snowflake on original unit. Replacement was already issued by Amazon. Review reflects initial defective item, not the replacement.

nrSummary.cause: Product durability issue — fading and coming apart after ~4 months
nrSummary.notes: Reviewer purchased in November 2025 and reports in April 2026 (approx. 4 months) that the item is fading fast and coming apart despite not being in direct sunlight. This is a durability complaint on a Barnyard Designs printed mat/doormat. The reviewer issued a broad brand warning.

nrSummary.cause: Blend sprouting — uneven germination across mixed seeds
nrSummary.notes: 2-star review on Fresh Salad Blend (Alfalfa, Broccoli, Radish, Mung Bean, Lentil). Customer reports different seeds sprouted at different times, leaving a mix of sprouts and unsprouted seeds at harvest. Stated intent to buy individual varieties next purchase. Mixed-blend sprouting naturally produces uneven germination — larger seeds (mung bean, lentil) sprout slower than smaller seeds (alfalfa, broccoli, radish). Listing does not currently disclose this timing variability.

nrSummary.cause: Germination failure (partial) — one or two varieties in blend fermented/rotted instead of sprouting
nrSummary.notes: Customer sprouted the Organic Salad Mix (SKU: SS-SALAD-8OZ, ASIN: B0DL79BPQW) in a quality container with adequate drainage. Most varieties sprouted successfully and were rated excellent; however, one or two varieties fermented/rotted in the same setup. Customer cannot identify which specific varieties failed. This is a known challenge with mixed sprouting blends — varieties with different optimal moisture levels or sprouting times can experience uneven results when grown together. Order placed March 10, reviewed March 27 — approximately 17 days, consistent with sprouting attempt timeline.

nrSummary.cause: Fulfillment complaint posted as product review — reviewer complains about missing items from order (lids, seeds), not product quality
nrSummary.notes: Customer purchased SS-SALAD-8OZ (ASIN B0DL79BPQW, seeds-only Salad Blend at 4.94). Review complains about not receiving "2 metal lids" and seeds — accessories only included in the "Salad w/ Jar" variant (JAR-SALAD-8OZ, B0DT2YGZNL, 4.95). The Amazon listing clearly labels each variant separately with distinct names and prices. Reviewer ends with "Other than that.. they work fine," confirming this is not a product quality complaint. This is fulfillment or order feedback, not a product review.

Reviewer C gave 1-star with title 'Not worth it' and body 'The seeds Don't sprout at the same consistency I do not recommend for the money you spend.' Product is SS-SALAD-8OZ (Fresh Salad Blend), a Tier A Seedboy SKU. Customer experienced inconsistent germination across the blend. This is likely a growing method issue (soaking time, drainage, rinse frequency) rather than seed quality failure.

nrSummary.cause: Germination failure — complete sprout failure despite following package directions and video tutorials
nrSummary.notes: Customer reports zero germination on the Fresh Salad Blend (SS-SALAD-8OZ) despite following package directions and watching instructional videos. No growing conditions disclosed (jar type, rinse frequency, temperature, water quality). Root cause cannot be confirmed — could be user error or batch quality issue. Review tone is strongly dismissive and discourages purchase. No return mentioned.

Customer reports 50°F growing environment, inconsistent sprouting, mixed germination rates, and use of soil. Salad sprouting blends require warmer temperatures and non-soil sprouting methods. No indication of defective or dead seeds.
Customer left a low-effort, non-specific review ("Not the best", "Would not order again") with no actionable product defect, performance issue, or policy-violating content mentioned.

Customer reported sprouts softening/spoiling. Superfood Blend contains mixed small seeds (broccoli, pak choi, clover, red kale, radish) that sprout at slightly different speeds. Customer likely waited for uniform length before harvest, leading to overgrowth and excess moisture in faster varieties.

nrSummary.cause: Expectation mismatch — sprout size vs. advertised
nrSummary.notes: Customer reports broccoli sprouts (SKU SS-BROCCO-8OZ) only grew to half the size advertised and required more work/effort than expected. Customer still ate the product and rated it 2 stars. Order placed April 4, 2026; review left May 6, 2026. Broccoli microgreen size is sensitive to harvest day, light exposure, and growing medium — common variability factor.

Customer (Pat V.) left a 1-star review on Organic Broccoli Sprouting Seeds 8 oz (SS-BROCCO-8OZ) reporting ~50% germination and thin stems on the sprouts that did emerge. Customer states experience growing sprouts and following instructions. Order placed March 30, 2026 — recent purchase, fresh seed expected. Legitimate complaint based on actual sprouting attempt.

nrSummary.cause: Below-expected germination rate — ~40% vs. reviewer's usual 75%+
nrSummary.notes: Experienced microgreens grower reports ~40% germination on broccoli seeds vs. their usual 75%+ from a different brand they typically use. Notes cracked seeds that never sprouted. Reviewer is trying sprouts and another tray of microgreens to determine if it was a one-off glitch. Taste was good from seeds that did grow. Review may be updated.

nrSummary.cause: Expectation mismatch — customer believed sprouting jar/equipment was included; received seeds only
nrSummary.notes: Customer purchased the Broccoli Sprouting Seeds (8 oz) expecting a full kit including a sprouting jar, based on product imagery and 'great for beginners' description. After delivery, she re-reviewed the listing and could not find any statement clarifying the jar is not included. As a self-identified beginner, she had chosen this product over cheaper options specifically because she believed it was a complete kit. This is an expectation mismatch rooted in a listing clarity gap, not a product defect.

nrSummary.cause: Off-label use — product used as dog remedy, not marketed for pets
nrSummary.notes: Customer used wheatgrass seeds to treat their dogs' upset stomachs. Dogs refused to eat the product despite it growing correctly. Customer explicitly states 'it was not the product's fault' and notes it grew quickly and was easy to maintain. Off-label use; product performed as intended. Rating reflects a use-case mismatch, not a product defect.
